name: Dutch East India Company (VOC) first public shares
magnitude_approx: n/a (context event: first widely traded joint-stock company)
trigger: Chartered trade monopoly funded by public subscription
contagion_channels: Amsterdam exchange trading of shares and later derivatives-like contracts

name: Tulip mania collapse
magnitude_approx: Bulb contract prices fell by more than 90% (scale and breadth debated by historians)
trigger: Speculative forward contracts on bulbs; buyer defaults
policy_response: Authorities proposed settling contracts at a fraction of face price

name: South Sea Bubble
magnitude_approx: South Sea shares fell roughly 85% from mid-1720 peak
trigger: Debt-for-equity scheme plus speculation
contagion_channels: Credit-funded stock buying; spillover to other joint-stock companies
policy_response: Bubble Act 1720; restructuring of company debt

name: Mississippi Bubble
magnitude_approx: Company shares fell more than 90% from peak
trigger: John Law's Mississippi Company and paper-money bank

name: Credit crisis of 1772 (Ayr Bank, East India Company)
magnitude_approx: Dozens of banks failed (not index-based)
trigger: Collapse of speculation in East India Company stock; failure of the Ayr Bank
contagion_channels: Interbank credit chains across London, Scotland, Amsterdam
policy_response: Bank of England credit extension; government support for the East India Company in 1773

name: Panic of 1792
magnitude_approx: n/a
trigger: Credit expansion and failure of speculator William Duer
contagion_channels: Failures spread through New York credit
policy_response: Treasury (Hamilton) bought securities and supported banks

name: Panic of 1837
magnitude_approx: Multi-year depression (n/a)
trigger: Land speculation, Specie Circular, cotton price fall
policy_response: No central bank response (second Bank of the US had lost its charter)

name: Panic of 1857
magnitude_approx: n/a
trigger: Failure of Ohio Life Insurance and Trust; railroad speculation
contagion_channels: Transatlantic spread via shipping and telegraph

name: Panic of 1873
magnitude_approx: NYSE closed for about 10 days after Jay Cooke & Co failed (Sep 18, 1873)
trigger: Railroad overbuilding; Vienna crash (May 1873); Jay Cooke failure

name: Panic of 1893
magnitude_approx: n/a
trigger: Gold reserve drain and railroad failures

name: Panic of 1907
magnitude_approx: DJIA roughly -48% from Jan 1906 peak to Nov 1907 low
trigger: Failed copper corner; run on Knickerbocker Trust (Oct 22)
contagion_channels: Trust bank runs; call-loan rate spikes
policy_response: J.P. Morgan-led private rescue pool; led to Federal Reserve Act (1913)

name: Wall Street Crash (Black Thursday Oct 24, Black Tuesday Oct 29)
magnitude_approx: DJIA roughly -89% from Sep 1929 peak to Jul 1932 trough
trigger: Margin-fueled speculation, tighter Fed policy, rich valuations
contagion_channels: Margin calls, bank failures, global trade collapse
policy_response: Initial bankers' pool; later Glass-Steagall and SEC (1933-34)

name: 1937-38 recession and bear market
magnitude_approx: DJIA roughly -49%
trigger: Fiscal and monetary tightening (reserve requirement increases)
policy_response: Policy reversal and renewed spending in 1938

name: Kennedy Slide
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -28%
trigger: Rich valuations; steel price confrontation

name: 1973-74 bear market and oil embargo
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -48%
trigger: Oil embargo (Oct 1973), Bretton Woods collapse, inflation

name: Black Monday
magnitude_approx: DJIA -22.6% in a single day
trigger: Portfolio insurance, program trading, valuations
contagion_channels: Futures and cash markets feeding each other; global selloff
policy_response: Fed liquidity statement; circuit breakers introduced afterward

name: Japan asset bubble burst
magnitude_approx: Nikkei roughly -80% by 2003 (about -82% at 2009 low)
trigger: BOJ tightening and real-estate lending curbs
contagion_channels: Bank balance sheets and non-performing loans

name: Black Wednesday / ERM crisis
magnitude_approx: Sterling forced out of the ERM; large depreciation over following months
trigger: Speculative attack on pegged currencies
policy_response: Rate hikes failed to hold peg; exit from ERM

name: Mexican peso crisis
magnitude_approx: Peso lost roughly 50% against USD in months
trigger: Peg abandoned amid reserve depletion

name: Asian financial crisis
magnitude_approx: Indonesian rupiah lost around 80% at worst; baht, won also collapsed
trigger: Thai baht float on Jul 2, 1997

name: Russian default and LTCM
magnitude_approx: LTCM lost roughly $4.6B; Fed-brokered private rescue in Sep 1998
trigger: Russian default and ruble devaluation
policy_response: NY Fed organized private recapitalization; Fed rate cuts

name: Dot-com bubble burst
magnitude_approx: Nasdaq Composite roughly -78%
trigger: Extreme valuations, rate hikes, earnings misses

name: 9/11 market closure
magnitude_approx: NYSE closed 4 sessions; DJIA about -7.1% on reopening (Sep 17)
trigger: Terrorist attack
policy_response: Fed rate cut and liquidity provision

name: Argentina default and devaluation
magnitude_approx: Among the largest sovereign defaults to that date (order of $80-100B)
trigger: Unsustainable currency board and debt

name: Quant quake
magnitude_approx: Sharp losses at market-neutral quant funds within days
trigger: Crowded positions and forced deleveraging

name: Global Financial Crisis (Lehman, Sep 15, 2008)
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -57% (Oct 2007 to Mar 2009)
trigger: Subprime mortgage losses; Lehman failure
contagion_channels: Interbank freeze, money market fund break, CDS/AIG

name: Flash Crash
magnitude_approx: DJIA roughly -9% intraday, mostly recovered within minutes
trigger: Large algorithmic sell order and liquidity withdrawal
policy_response: Limit up-limit down rules and circuit breaker reforms

name: Eurozone sovereign debt crisis
magnitude_approx: Bailouts for Greece, Ireland, Portugal; peripheral yields spiked
trigger: Greek deficit revelations

name: US credit rating downgrade
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -6.7% on Aug 8
trigger: S&P downgrade of US to AA+

name: Taper tantrum
magnitude_approx: 10Y Treasury yield rose from about 1.6% to about 3% over months; EM currencies sold off
trigger: Fed signal of QE tapering

name: Swiss franc shock
magnitude_approx: EUR/CHF fell roughly 30% intraday
trigger: SNB removed euro floor

name: China stock market crash
magnitude_approx: Shanghai Composite roughly -43%; about -8.5% on Aug 24
trigger: Leveraged retail margin trading; Aug 11 yuan devaluation

name: Brexit referendum
magnitude_approx: GBP roughly -8% in one day (largest one-day move in decades)
trigger: Referendum result against polls

name: Volmageddon
magnitude_approx: VIX roughly doubled in a day; XIV collapsed; DJIA about -4.6% on Feb 5
trigger: Short-volatility product rebalancing
contagion_channels: Equities and vol ETPs feeding each other

name: Q4 2018 selloff
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -19.8%
trigger: Fed tightening and trade war

name: Repo market spike
magnitude_approx: Overnight repo rates spiked to around 10%
trigger: Tax date plus Treasury settlement draining reserves
policy_response: Fed repo operations and bill purchases

name: COVID-19 crash
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -34% in 33 days
trigger: Pandemic lockdowns
policy_response: Fed cuts to zero, unlimited QE, CARES Act

name: WTI negative price
magnitude_approx: May WTI contract settled around -$37
trigger: Storage constraints and demand collapse

name: GameStop short squeeze
magnitude_approx: GME rose more than 1,500% in January 2021
trigger: Retail coordination on Reddit; gamma squeeze; short covering
contagion_channels: Hedge fund deleveraging; broker trading restrictions

name: Archegos collapse
magnitude_approx: Over $20B of positions liquidated; Credit Suisse lost about $5.5B
trigger: Concentrated leverage via total return swaps; margin call

name: 2022 inflation bear market
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -25%; bonds had a historically bad year
trigger: Fed rate hikes, inflation, war in Ukraine (from Feb 24, 2022)

name: UK gilt crisis
magnitude_approx: Long gilt yields rose by more than 1 percentage point within days
trigger: Mini-budget and pension LDI leverage
contagion_channels: LDI margin calls forcing gilt sales

name: Terra/Luna collapse
magnitude_approx: UST depegged; LUNA lost over 99%; tens of billions in value lost
trigger: Algorithmic stablecoin death spiral

name: FTX collapse
magnitude_approx: FTX filed for Chapter 11 on Nov 11, 2022
trigger: Balance sheet leak and withdrawal run

name: SVB, Signature and Credit Suisse
magnitude_approx: SVB failed Mar 10, 2023; regional bank index fell sharply; UBS acquired Credit Suisse Mar 19
trigger: Held-to-maturity losses, uninsured deposits, social-media-fueled run
policy_response: FDIC systemic risk exception; Fed BTFP

name: Yen carry trade unwind
magnitude_approx: Nikkei -12.4% in a day; VIX spiked above 60 intraday
trigger: BOJ hike and weak US jobs data

name: April 2025 tariff shock
magnitude_approx: S&P 500 roughly -19% peak to trough
trigger: US tariff announcements (Apr 2)
